name: Windows Disk & System
description: Protects against catastrophic Windows disk/system operations: \ `vssadmin delete shadows` / `wmic shadowcopy delete` (Volume Shadow Copy \ destruction), `diskpart`, `Format-Volume`, `Clear-Disk`, `Remove-Partition`, \ `Initialize-Disk`, `Reset-PhysicalDisk`, `cipher /w`, and `bcdedit /delete`.

destructive_patterns.name: vssadmin-delete-shadows
destructive_patterns.description: vssadmin delete shadows destroys Volume Shadow Copies (System Restore + backups).
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`vssadmin delete shadows` deletes the Volume Shadow Copies on a volume — the snapshots \ that back System Restore, Previous Versions, and many backup tools. With `/all /quiet` \ it removes every shadow copy with no prompt. This is one of the first things ransomware \ does, and run by accident it silently removes the main local recovery path.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - vssadmin list shadows: review what exists before deleting anything \ - Take a fresh backup (wbadmin / your backup tool) instead of deleting recovery points

destructive_patterns.name: wmic-shadowcopy-delete
destructive_patterns.description: wmic shadowcopy delete destroys Volume Shadow Copies.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`wmic shadowcopy delete` is an alternate way to destroy Volume Shadow Copies (the same \ snapshots that back System Restore and backups). Like `vssadmin delete shadows` it is a \ common ransomware step and an irreversible loss of local recovery.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - wmic shadowcopy list / vssadmin list shadows: inspect first \ - Back up before removing any recovery points

destructive_patterns.name: diskpart
destructive_patterns.description: diskpart with clean/delete/format/script reconfigures or wipes disks and partitions.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`diskpart` is the low-level disk-partitioning tool. Driven by a script (`/s file.txt`) or \ with `clean`/`delete partition`/`delete volume`/`format`, it wipes partition tables and \ volumes — a wrong disk number destroys the wrong drive irreversibly. A non-interactive \ agent has no confirmation prompt.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - diskpart -> `list disk` / `list volume`: confirm the exact target first \ - Use Get-Disk/Get-Partition to inspect before any clean/delete

destructive_patterns.name: format-volume
destructive_patterns.description: Format-Volume erases a volume's filesystem and data.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`Format-Volume` re-creates the filesystem on a volume, destroying all data on it. A wrong \ drive letter or disk number formats the wrong volume. There is no Recycle Bin for a \ format.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Get-Volume / Get-Partition: confirm the exact target first \ - Back up the volume before any format

destructive_patterns.name: clear-disk
destructive_patterns.description: Clear-Disk removes all partitions and data from a disk.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`Clear-Disk` wipes a whole physical disk — with `-RemoveData -RemoveOEM` it deletes every \ partition (including recovery/OEM) and all data. A wrong disk number destroys the wrong \ drive irreversibly.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Get-Disk: confirm the disk number and that it is the intended target \ - Back up before clearing; consider removing a single partition instead

destructive_patterns.name: remove-partition
destructive_patterns.description: Remove-Partition deletes a partition and its data.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`Remove-Partition` deletes a partition and everything on it. Targeting the wrong disk or \ partition number destroys live data with no undo.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Get-Partition: confirm the disk/partition numbers first \ - Back up the partition's data before removing it

destructive_patterns.name: initialize-or-reset-disk
destructive_patterns.description: Initialize-Disk / Reset-PhysicalDisk wipe disk metadata and data.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`Initialize-Disk` re-initializes a disk's partition style and `Reset-PhysicalDisk` resets \ a physical disk — both discard existing partitioning/data on the target. On a disk that \ already holds data this is destructive and easy to point at the wrong disk.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Get-Disk: confirm the disk is empty / the intended target first \ - Back up before initializing or resetting

destructive_patterns.name: cipher-wipe
destructive_patterns.description: cipher /w overwrites free space, making deleted files unrecoverable.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`cipher /w:<path>` overwrites all free space on the volume, permanently destroying the \ recoverability of any previously deleted files. It is slow, irreversible, and usually run \ by mistake when a simple delete was intended.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - If you only need to remove a file, delete it normally \ - Reserve free-space wiping for decommissioning, after backups are confirmed

destructive_patterns.name: bcdedit-delete
destructive_patterns.description: bcdedit /delete removes a boot configuration entry.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
`bcdedit /delete` (and `/deletevalue`) removes Boot Configuration Data entries. A wrong \ entry can leave the machine unbootable. Boot config should be changed deliberately, not \ as part of a cleanup.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - bcdedit /enum: review the current boot entries first \ - Export with `bcdedit /export` before modifying anything
